issues.description: The solution repository changes the constructor visibility of PersonService from public to private and introduces a private static singleton instance (INSTANCE). The template defines a public constructor (allowing Spring to instantiate the service as a bean), while the solution makes the constructor private and adds INSTANCE = new PersonService(). This is a structural change that conflicts with the Spring @Service usage and the template's design: Spring cannot create a bean from a class with a private no-arg constructor, so the change breaks the intended instantiation model and will confuse students about how the service is supposed to be provided.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore a public no-argument constructor on PersonService and remove the private singleton INSTANCE and private constructor. Keep PersonService as a regular Spring @Service bean (public constructor) and implement only the intended getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) sorting logic. This preserves the Spring bean model and aligns with the template and problem instructions.

issues.description: The solution repository adds new static attributes and accessor methods (INSTANCE, getInstance(), getAllPersonsStatic()) to PersonService that are not present in the template and that change the class's attributes and API. The problem statement explicitly warns not to change the attributes of PersonService. Adding these static members alters the class structure and could mislead students about the expected class shape and how to interact with it (and it may cause tests to fail).
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the added static INSTANCE field and the extra static methods (getInstance(), getAllPersonsStatic()) from the solution's PersonService. The class should retain the single instance field 'private final List<Person> persons' and a public constructor as in the template. Only implement the missing getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) functionality; do not add or remove class-level attributes or change the bean instantiation model.
